title: A night in Ramadan
hook: at forty, in Ramadan, the angel comes (97:1; 2:185)

segments.voice: Yesterday: tahannuth, worship in seclusion on the mountain, with provisions packed by Khadijah. Your line was: alone with the one.

One night on that mountain is different from all the others he spent there. The Qur'an doesn't give its date. It gives its month, and its name, and says it is better than a thousand months. The Prophet told his companions to look for it near the end of Ramadan, and the looking goes on: people stay awake through those last nights, praying and reading, not sure which night it is. Today: a night in Ramadan.
screen: `ONE NIGHT UNLIKE THE OTHERS.` → `A MONTH AND A NAME, NO DATE.` → `STILL WATCHED FOR.`

segments.voice: Start with the month. The Qur'an names it in surah two. Pickthall's translation: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind." That's why the fast is in Ramadan: it's the month the book arrived. Then the night. A short surah, the ninety-seventh, opens: "Lo! We revealed it on the Night of Power." And it says: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." The angels and the Spirit come down that night, it says, and it is peace until dawn. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was forty when revelation began: a man of forty, in a cave in the dark, on a night that would get its own surah. What exactly came down? Scholars answer in more than one way. Some, following a report from Ibn 'Abbas, say the whole Qur'an was sent down that night to the nearest heaven, then revealed to the Prophet piece by piece over the years. Others focus on this night as the beginning, when the first verses came to him in the cave. Either way, the text is clear about the night and silent about its date. In Sahih al-Bukhari, he tells his companions to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten of Ramadan. In Muslim teaching the Night of Power comes round again every Ramadan, and so the night it came is sought each year.
screen: `THE MONTH THE BOOK ARRIVED.` · `BETTER THAN A THOUSAND MONTHS.` · `WHAT CAME DOWN THAT NIGHT.` · `SEEK IT IN THE ODD NIGHTS.` · then, large: `THE NIGHT IT CAME.`

segments.voice: Sit for a moment as if it were the hour before dawn: the house asleep, the dark outside, nothing asking anything of you. If you pray, there is a night prayer called tahajjud, and even two short units of it are a way to keep this hour; if you don't, just keep the quiet company a while.
Ramadan, the month the Qur'an itself names as when it was revealed, home to the hidden Night of Power, better than a thousand months. Today's word.
Your line: the night it came. Its date is hidden, so the looking goes on. Day seven hundred twenty-three, done.

howItsDone: Muslims seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd ones, staying up in prayer, recitation and supplication, and some spend those nights in i'tikaf in the mosque.

chat.says: Do Muslims know the exact date of the Night of Power?
options: Not for certain; he said to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.
Yes; the Qur'an names the date as the first night of Ramadan.
Yes; it falls on the night of the Prophet's birthday each year.
chat.meaning: The Qur'an gives the month and the name but not the date; in Bukhari he says to seek it in the odd nights of the last ten.

Night of Power.meaning: Laylat al-Qadr, better than a thousand months

Ramadan.meaning: the month of fasting, when the Qur'an was revealed

Ibn 'Abbas.meaning: the Prophet's cousin, an early interpreter of the Qur'an

tahajjud.meaning: a voluntary prayer in the night

notes: Age forty is attributed to a report in Sahih al-Bukhari (Ibn 'Abbas); confirm the number 3902 (or 3851).
Pickthall 2:185, 97:1 and 97:3 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording and capitalization.
The Ibn 'Abbas report (whole Qur'an to the nearest heaven, bayt al-'izzah, then piecemeal) is cited via tafsir and al-Hakim/al-Nasa'i; confirm the best citation.
Hook: 'Muslims have been watching for it ever since, every Ramadan' is a general description of practice; confirm acceptable.
Communities differ over which odd night they especially mark (the 27th is widely kept; Shia communities give weight to the 19th, 21st and 23rd); left out of the script by the claims rule.
Practice mentions tahajjud and 'two short units'; confirm wording as an invitation.

Editor: 97:3 no longer glossed as 'worth more than a lifetime' (the text says a thousand months); hook and teach no longer claim what 'Muslims' as a whole do each Ramadan, and tie the search to the Bukhari 2017 instruction; fixed the garbled practice line 'If you pray, Muslims pray...'; dropped 'picture'; fork option no longer says 'the date most people say'.

Audit: 'sought as if it were still coming' implied the yearly return of the Night of Power is a pretense; Muslim teaching holds it recurs each Ramadan, so the line now says that descriptively. Keeper to confirm phrasing.
